picks.name: anime.js v4 (with Three.js adapter)
picks.gives: choreography + native Three.js adapter animates Object3D/material/camera directly — good for orb hover/idle, holo card motion, title reveal inside the scene
picks.where: import 'animejs/adapters/three' side-effect, then animate() any Object3D
picks.risk: ~42KB gzip full lib; three-adapter is new in v4, smaller track record

picks.name: Motion (formerly Framer Motion)
picks.licenseEvidence: raw LICENSE.md in repo root confirms MIT
picks.gives: declarative variants/stagger orchestration for DOM/SVG choreography (title reveal overlay UI)
picks.where: React DOM/SVG layer only; no maintained Three.js binding (framer-motion-3d is stale)
picks.risk: ~34KB gzip full; doesn't touch WebGL meshes directly, needs a separate approach for orb/holo cards in-canvas

picks.name: dotlottie-web (LottieFiles)
picks.licenseEvidence: github license badge + package.json; Rust/WASM core, MIT throughout
picks.gives: Lottie/.lottie playback (After-Effects authored splash/lamp/title vector sequences)
picks.where: renders to its own <canvas>; bridge into scene via CanvasTexture or as a DOM overlay
picks.risk: adds ~380KB+ WASM asset loaded async, separate render surface from WebGL canvas

picks.name: lottie-web (Airbnb)
picks.gives: mature SVG/canvas Lottie player, huge library of existing AE-exported JSON examples
picks.where: DOM/SVG or canvas renderer, same overlay caveat as dotlottie
picks.risk: release cadence has slowed vs dotlottie-web; heavier SVG DOM renderer by default

picks.name: Rive (rive-runtime + @rive-app/react-canvas)
picks.gives: state-machine driven vector animation — strong fit for interactive hover/idle orb avatar and title-reveal blending
picks.where: own canvas/WebGL2 surface; overlay or CanvasTexture bridge into three scene
picks.risk: authoring requires the proprietary Rive desktop editor (runtime code is MIT, tooling is not); webgl2 variant ships ~0.9MB gzip WASM, use canvas-lite for smaller

picks.name: pixi.js AnimatedSprite
picks.licenseEvidence: raw LICENSE at pixijs/pixijs dev branch confirmed MIT
picks.gives: ready-made sprite-sheet frame player (AnimatedSprite class, animationSpeed, loop) for pixel-art avatar motion packs
picks.where: separate 2D/WebGL renderer; use as CanvasTexture source for a three.js plane or as a DOM overlay canvas
picks.risk: pulls in a second WebGL context/renderer just for sprite playback — only worth it for many sprites/atlases

picks.name: three.js native texture offset/repeat pattern
picks.licenseEvidence: three.js is already a project dependency (MIT LICENSE at repo root)
picks.gives: sprite-sheet playback directly on a THREE.Mesh/Sprite by stepping texture.offset/.repeat per frame — zero extra bundle cost
picks.where: already-imported three.js Texture API, no new dependency
picks.risk: no built-in AnimatedSprite class — you write the frame-stepping/uv-offset loop yourself (~20 lines)

rejected.name: GSAP
rejected.license: Webflow Standard "No Charge" GSAP License (exception, not OSI)
rejected.licenseEvidence: gsap.com/community/standard-license/ — free commercial use; prohibits building no-code visual-animation competitors to Webflow
rejected.gives: choreographed timelines/sequencing for splash dissolve, lamp ignite, title reveal
rejected.where: npm import, runs fine in Tauri WebView (no Node at runtime)
rejected.risk: license restricts building visual-animation-builder tools; not MIT/Apache/CC0 but explicitly pre-approved exception
rejected.reason: license not allowed: Webflow Standard "No Charge" GSAP License (exception, not OSI)
rejected.rejectedBy: license-gate: license not allowed: Webflow Standard "No Charge" GSAP License (exception, not OSI)

rejected.name: framer-motion-3d
rejected.reason: unmaintained/stale, superseded by react-three-fiber + drei patterns; don't use for Three.js meshes

rejected.name: Spine Runtimes
rejected.reason: runtime code is permissive but authoring/export requires a paid Spine editor license — not a clean MIT/Apache/CC0 pipeline

rejected.name: CreateJS / EaselJS
rejected.reason: MIT but effectively unmaintained (no commits in years); superseded by pixi.js for sprite playback

rejected.name: Velocity.js
rejected.reason: unmaintained since ~2020, no reason to pick over GSAP/anime.js for this stack

rejected.name: react-spring
rejected.reason: redundant given GSAP (timelines) + anime.js (Three.js adapter) already cover choreography and physics springs

rejected.name: Phaser
rejected.reason: MIT but a full game engine — far too heavy just for sprite-sheet playback of a single avatar

rejected.name: three-SpriteMixer
rejected.reason: tiny wrapper around the same texture-offset trick, low activity — just implement the pattern natively instead

top: GSAP (exception license) for splash/lamp/title choreography timelines — already chosen, verified terms above.
anime.js v4's native Three.js adapter for in-scene choreography (orb hover/idle, holo cards) without leaving WebGL.
Native three.js texture-offset pattern (zero new deps) for pixel-art sprite-sheet playback; reach for pixi.js AnimatedSprite only if you need many atlases via a second canvas layer.

Stack: Tauri 2 + React + TS + three 0.186.
